land.text: the Kingdom of Hungary and the lands its government claimed, minus Croatia-Slavonia

predecessors.note: The Austrian Empire dossier of this project records the contest over this zone from December 1848 to August 1849 against counterpart hungarian-nationalists.

land.text: 'Habsburg power was restored and Hungary was placed under martial law'; Vojvodina 'became an Austrian Crown Land'

successors.note: Not one state but the Austrian Empire's restored lands; the page adds that after the fall of the revolution 'the Kingdom of Hungary was carved up into five independent military districts' (infobox).

capitals.name: Pest
capitals.note: Budapest did not exist as one city; the page says the combined armies 'entered Pest on 5 January 1849' and that the government evacuated Pest for Debrecen (dated by its context to late December 1848).

capitals.name: Debrecen
capitals.note: 'The Hungarian government evacuated Pest for Debrecen.' The page says Buda castle was recaptured on 21 May 1849; where the government sat after that is not on the page.

correction.text: The Hungarian lands without Transylvania ('By December 1848, Austrian General Puchner had taken control of Transylvania, except for Haromszek') and without the Serb-held south ('Serb reinforcements soon turned the tide, capturing much of Southern Banat and Backa'); Croatia is already outside the 1849 shape ('the Croats rebelled against the Hungarians and declared their loyalty to Austria')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for December 1848, when Windisch-Gratz crossed into Hungary (14 December); Cliopatria's row begins in 1849. The 1849 shape contains 215 of 220 Transylvania cells and 44 Serbian (Vojvodina) cells that the page puts in Austrian or Serb hands by the end of 1848.

correction.text: The shape unchanged for 1849 only: after the surrender of 1849 'Habsburg power was restored and Hungary was placed under martial law', so Cliopatria's 1850-1852 years belong to the Austrian Empire

keyframe_review.note: 271,818 km2 = 1,054 cells: Hungary 363 of 366, Slovakia 182 of 195, Transylvania 215 of 220, Romania (with the Banat and Crisana) 391, Serbia (Vojvodina) 44, Ukraine (Transcarpathia) 53, Croatia 3. That is the historic Kingdom of Hungary without Croatia-Slavonia, the extent the revolution claimed; the page gives no area and no spring-1849 front line (it says only that Hungary 'retained Komarom and others west of the Tisza River, while the east mostly remained imperial'). The Austrian Empire dossier already applies its 1853 outline to 1849-1852 and carries this zone as contested until August 1849.

correction.text: Hungary within its present frontier (91,985 km2, the same outline as the People's Republic's 1950-1955 and 1958 shapes), belonging to the Hungarian People's Republic through 1956-1957

keyframe_review.note: The 1956-1957 shape is the whole of Hungary, equal in area to the People's Republic's 1950-1955 shape, and Cliopatria's Hungarian People's Republic row has a gap exactly in 1956-1957. The 1956 page treats the revolution as an uprising inside the Hungarian People's Republic ('the Hungarian People's Republic (1949-1989)'), with Kadar's regime a continuation of that state: revolutionary workers' councils 'assumed government power' and Imre Nagy's government (24 October) declared the Warsaw Pact withdrawal on 1 November, but no separate state held separate land. The Hungarian People's Republic dossier, not this one, should draw Hungary in 1956-1957.

region.text: the Hungarian lands held against the Austrian invasion

ledger.note: December 1848: the Hungarian revolutionary government takes the field against Vienna. The revolution began on 15 March 1848 ('revolution broke out in Buda on 15 March'; April laws given royal assent on 10 April); 'On December 14, Austrian forces led by Windisch-Gratz crossed into Hungary'. The page names no founding act, so the month is that of the break with the crown in arms, chosen to match the Austrian Empire dossier's contest from December 1848.
14 December 1848: Austria invades Hungary. 'On December 14, Austrian forces led by Windisch-Gratz crossed into Hungary.'

Late December 1848: 'The Hungarian government evacuated Pest for Debrecen' (destination in identity.capitals); the page orders this after the Battle of Mor on 30 December and the entry into Pest on 5 January 1849, so the month is a reading.
5 January 1849: the capital falls. 'the combined Bohemian and Croatian armies entered Pest on 5 January 1849.'

April 1849: Kossuth issues the Declaration of Independence and the revolutionary government becomes an independent state. 'In April 1849, when the Hungarians had won multiple successes ... Kossuth issued the celebrated Hungarian Declaration of Independence'; Habsburg-Lorraine 'had forfeited the Hungarian throne'. The page gives no day and does not name Debrecen with the sentence.
21 May 1849: the Hungarians retake Buda. 'recapture of Buda castle, finally successful on 21 May 1849.'

region.text: the Hungarian lands, entered by the Russian army

ledger.note: 1849: Russia intervenes. 'The hopes of ultimate success were, however, frustrated by the intervention of Russia', which 'sent a 200,000 strong army with 80,000 auxiliary forces'; the page gives no month for the entry; June is a bridge between the Warsaw meeting of Franz Joseph and the Tsar on 21 May 1849 and the August surrender.
August 1849: 'on 11 August, Kossuth abdicated in favor of Gorgey', who then 'capitulated at Vilagos ... to the Russians, who handed over the army to the Austrians'.

August 1849: the revolutionary army surrenders. The page dates Kossuth's abdication (11 August) but gives no date for Gorgey's capitulation at Vilagos (the Austrian Empire dossier gives 13 August from another page); the infobox runs the revolution to 4 October 1849.

region.text: Hungary, Transylvania and the Banat returned to Habsburg rule

ledger.note: August 1849: the Hungarian lands pass back to Vienna. 'Habsburg power was restored and Hungary was placed under martial law'; 'After the fall of the Hungarian revolution in 1849, Vojvodina became an Austrian Crown Land'.
August 1849: the Hungarian revolutionary state ends with Kossuth's abdication and the capitulation at Vilagos.

wars.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1848

zones.text: the Hungarian lands, from the Austrian crossing of 14 December 1848 to the surrender of August 1849

wars.outcome: Austro-Russian victory (infobox); Habsburg power was restored and Hungary placed under martial law; Vojvodina became an Austrian Crown Land.
wars.note: Infobox dates 15 March 1848 - 4 October 1849; the page's front-line detail is thin (Transylvania Austrian by December 1848 except Haromszek, southern Banat and Backa taken by Serbs, Croatia loyal to Austria, a Slovak council seceding).

certainty.note: The revolution's hold moved with the front (Transylvania and the south in Austrian or Serb hands by December 1848, Pest lost 5 January and Buda retaken 21 May 1849); the drawn outline is the claimed extent, not a surveyed frontier.

sources.title: Hungarian Revolution of 1848
sources.note: Infobox dates, 14 December 1848 crossing, 5 January 1849 Pest, Declaration of Independence (April 1849), 21 May Buda, Russian intervention, Kossuth's abdication (11 August), martial law, territory notes.

sources.title: Hungarian Revolution of 1956
sources.note: Used for the second Cliopatria shape (1956-1957): the revolution inside the Hungarian People's Republic, 23 October - 11 November 1956.

notes: TWO EPISODES, ONE CLIOPATRIA ROW. 'Hungarian Nationalists' (1849-1957) holds two unrelated shapes. The 1849-1852 shape is the Hungarian revolutionary state of the 1848-49 war, written here as a rebel state (December 1848 - August 1849). The 1956-1957 shape (91,985 km2) is the whole of Hungary in the two years where Cliopatria's Hungarian People's Republic row has a gap (1950-1955, then 1958-1989); the 1956 page treats the revolution as an uprising inside that People's Republic, so the shape is marked wrong and the hungarian-people-s-republic dossier (another batch) should draw Hungary through 1956-1957. WIKIDATA. Cliopatria gives Q28513 (Austria-Hungary) for this row, for austria-hungary and for hungary: they are different states, so this dossier is separate from austria-hungary and leaves wikidata null; the Wikipedia field 'Austria-Hungary' is likewise not this state (the Hungarian Revolution of 1848 page is linked). DATES. The page dates the Austrian crossing (14 December 1848), the fall of Pest (5 January 1849), Kossuth's abdication (11 August) and Buda (21 May 1849); it gives no day for the Declaration of Independence (April 1849), no date for Vilagos, Temesvar or Komarom and no June date for the Russian entry, so those are dated only as far as the page goes. The ruler strip is omitted (Kossuth as head of state is on the page but no list). Counterpart slugs: austrian-empire (its ledger already pairs with this row), russian-empire. States this batch did not open: the Croatian and Serb Vojvodina movements, Transylvanian Saxon and Romanian forces.
